context.context_requirement: Known compiler graph shape, valid homogeneous relationship, supported finite provider shape, explicit claim and consumer scope.

concepts.normative: Select every Entity and every explicit owns edge between Entities in one validated compiled project; preserve exact project and source identities.
concepts.formal: V = all Entity selectors in G.nodes; E = {(u,v) | an explicit G.relationships edge has relationship = owns, source u and target v}. Require 1 <= |V| <= 64.
concepts.plain: Use the whole project Entity graph, keeping only authored owns links.
concepts.example: inventory:A owns inventory:B; inventory:B owns inventory:C.
concepts.boundary: No generated owned-by edges, belongs-to substitution, inferred ownership, silent truncation, or scope filtering. Parallel owns records may map to one ordered pair only if every original edge ID is retained in provenance.

concepts.normative: One explicitly selected source Entity must reach one explicitly selected target Entity by a path containing at least one selected owns edge.
concepts.formal: D = {reachability(source,target)}; |D| = 1; claim true iff (source,target) is in E+ (positive transitive closure). Both endpoints must belong to V.
concepts.plain: Follow one or more owns arrows from the named source to the named target.
concepts.example: A -> B -> C satisfies A reaches C; removing B -> C makes the same claim false.
concepts.boundary: A equals C is insufficient by itself; a real nonempty cycle may satisfy self-reachability. This is an additional audit claim, not one of the compiler built-in obligation IDs and not a new normative transitivity rule for owns.

concepts.normative: Bind the exact source snapshot, compiled graph, profile, query, projection, identifier map, runtime and tool identities, raw positive evidence and broken-edge control to one candidate epoch.
concepts.formal: Bundle identity = SHA256(canonical manifest of named inputs, outputs, dependencies and their SHA256 digests); all required references must equal consumer-supplied expected identities.
concepts.plain: The evidence must describe exactly the graph and question the caller asked about.
concepts.example: Evidence for A -> B -> C cannot be reused after removing B -> C from the caller-pinned source snapshot.
concepts.boundary: Canonical byte encoding and manifest fields are E02 design work. Hash consistency is not origin authentication. Trusted compiler, host and read-only caller snapshot remain assumptions; all provider-writable workspace bytes are untrusted inputs.

concepts.normative: The candidate consumer dsv2-owns-reachability-consumer-v1 independently reconstructs the selected graph, compares the provider model, checks positive and negative evidence, and reports every required condition before aggregating.
concepts.formal: PASS iff every required condition is evaluated and satisfied. BLOCK iff any evaluable condition fails. Otherwise not_evaluable. BLOCK takes aggregate precedence; unknown dependent conditions stay not_evaluable.
concepts.plain: A separate reader checks the graph and evidence itself, and says why it passes, fails, or cannot yet be checked.
concepts.example: Missing evidence is not_evaluable; stale digest or a reported success contradicted by the graph is BLOCK; all checks satisfied is bounded PASS.
concepts.boundary: Consumer is a proposed component, not an existing deployed service. It must not import producer projection/verdict logic or EVF adapter reachability functions. Its receipt grants no approval or operational effect.

profile.runtime_binding: Pin exact supported Souffle executable and explicit runtime grant at E02/E03; no ambient PATH selection or unsafe fallback.
profile.identifier_map: Sort unique (feature_id,node_id) tuples using an explicitly fixed byte ordering in E02; assign N0..N63 with a bijective reverse map. Reject ambiguous compiler selector identities.
profile.projection_policy: All project Entity nodes and all explicit owns edges; retain source edge IDs, endpoints and scope. Sort and deduplicate provider pairs with complete reverse provenance; never drop graph nodes to meet the bound.
profile.selected_route_rationale: Entity-to-Entity owns supports a multi-hop graph without relying on pending UI profile decisions. Souffle uses the existing bounded graph protocol. No factory-result conversion or TLC dependency is required for this first slice.

denominators.note: Control and integrity conditions never enlarge or discharge unrelated compiler obligations.

acceptance_conditions.meaning: Independent reconstruction equals the full selected Entity/owns projection and reversible ID map.
Successful contained Souffle execution reports no violation for the exact positive graph, and independent reachability agrees.
Remove all incoming edges to the selected target from the normalized graph; native evidence and independent evaluation both report the selected source as a violation.
Required raw records and digests exist, parse, match the exact run and tool identities, and contain no contradictory or extra claims.
Consumer implementation and dependency closure are separately reviewed; producer acceptance is not its oracle.

verdicts.PASS: All six required conditions evaluated and satisfied; supports only the selected finite reachability claim.
verdicts.BLOCK: Any observed invalid schema, stale identity, unsupported bound, counterexample, mapping mismatch, evidence contradiction, surviving negative control or forbidden provider/claim.
verdicts.not_evaluable: A required result cannot be evaluated because source/evidence/runtime is unavailable, execution times out, containment cannot start, or prerequisite implementation is absent.
verdicts.aggregation: Collect all non-effectful checks; BLOCK if any fails, otherwise not_evaluable if any is unevaluable, otherwise PASS. Preserve each condition and causal reason. Never run dependent effects to collect more results.

nodes.meaning: Answer one finite authored-owns reachability question
